sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four statements or pairs of ½ mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or arrange in sequence).

questions.q: Match the careers in Column I with the area in Column II: (A) Event manager (B) Staff at a showroom (C) Day care in school for young children (D) Home-based craft centre; (i) Teaching (ii) Arts and crafts (iii) Resource manager and consumer education (iv) Interior decoration.

Match the columns: (A) Communication and extension (B) Housekeeping (C) Interior decorator (D) Dress designing; (i) Boutique (ii) Media production and management (iii) Staff at hotels (iv) Furniture designer.

State True or False: (i) Home Science teaches both the art and the science of managing a home. (ii) Home Science is only for girls. (iii) A person who owns and finances an enterprise is self-employed. (iv) The school course in Home Science is enough to get a specialised job.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False – it is for both boys and girls. (iii) True. (iv) False – it gives only basic knowledge; advanced courses are needed.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Working for another person for a salary is ______ employment. (ii) Running your own boutique is ______. (iii) Home Science draws content from science and ______ disciplines. (iv) The five specialisation areas include Food and Nutrition and ______ and Extension.
Classify as wage employment (WE) or self-employment (SE): (i) Pre-school teacher (ii) Owner of a home accessories showroom (iii) Production unit staff (iv) Conducting hobby classes.

Match the columns: (A) Food and Nutrition (B) Resource Management (C) Fabric and Apparel Science (D) Human Development; (i) Garment designing (ii) Institutional food service (iii) Care of special children (iv) Interior decoration.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Name any four wage-employment opportunities related to foods and nutrition.
questions.answer: Staff in a canteen or restaurant; cook; service staff; staff in a food production unit (preservation, bakery or confectionery); in-charge of a community centre or service.

questions.q: Mention any four self-employment opportunities available in the field of foods and nutrition.
questions.answer: Owner of a canteen, restaurant or tea/coffee shop; food service from home; conducting hobby classes; home-based production of preserved foods or bakery items; owner of a production unit.

questions.q: Name two self-employment opportunities for the youth in interior decoration.
questions.answer: Working as an interior designer, furniture designer, showroom or shop owner, show-case and window display designer, running a home-based craft centre or conducting hobby courses (any two).

questions.q: Give any four reasons why Home Science is relevant to both boys and girls.
questions.answer: Both share household responsibilities; both need to manage resources; problems are solved together by family members; it offers varied vocational and professional avenues to both; joint knowledge and skills raise the standard of living.

questions.q: Name any four home-based self-employment opportunities for Home Science students.
questions.answer: Boutique or tailoring from home; catering or tiffin service; creche or day care; tuitions or hobby classes; paying-guest service; home-based craft centre; production of pickles, jams or bakery items.

questions.q: List the five areas of specialisation in Home Science.
questions.answer: Food and Nutrition; Resource Management; Fabric and Apparel Science; Human Development; Communication and Extension.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain how Home Science is both an art and a science with two examples.
questions.answer: Home Science is the art of managing resources efficiently and the science of achieving a healthy, happy home. Example 1: learning the nutrients the body needs and their functions is the science; selecting dishes that give them and serving them attractively so that the family eats the right food is the art. Example 2: knowing how germs are removed by soap is science; keeping the house clean and tidy in an aesthetic way is art. It also draws on physics, chemistry, biology, economics, sociology and psychology.

questions.q: Distinguish between wage employment and self-employment with two examples each.
questions.answer: Wage employment means working for another person and receiving a wage or salary, e.g. staff in a hotel, a boutique or a production unit. Self-employment means that you own, run and finance the enterprise, e.g. owner of a boutique, a creche or a catering unit. A tailor who sets up his own shop is self-employed; if he works in a garment factory for a salary he is in wage employment.

questions.q: Why do people say that gender-based roles no longer hold in managing a home? Give three reasons.
questions.answer: Today more women work outside the home, so the responsibilities of home and family have to be shared. Both men and women need to manage resources like time, energy and money. Problems are best solved together by all members. Home Science also opens equal careers for boys and girls.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Name the five areas of specialisation of Home Science and give two examples of further specialisation in each.
questions.answer: (1) Food and Nutrition – food science, clinical nutrition, community nutrition, institutional food service. (2) Resource Management – housing and equipment, interior decoration, consumer education. (3) Fabric and Apparel Science – clothing construction, textile science, garment designing, care and maintenance of clothes. (4) Human Development – child welfare, adolescence and family guidance, care of the elderly and special children. (5) Communication and Extension – media for communication, programme planning and evaluation, training and capacity building, management of community service organisations. These are studied at graduate and post-graduate level.

questions.q: List five opportunities each for wage employment and self-employment in the field of Home Science (any areas).
questions.answer: Wage employment: staff in a canteen or restaurant; staff at a hotel or guest house; staff in an export house or boutique; creche or school teacher; staff in a retail outlet or event management firm; researcher in a development organisation. Self-employment: owner of a canteen or restaurant; owner of a boutique; interior or furniture designer with own shop; owner of a creche or day care; conducting hobby classes or tuitions at home; home-based production centre; event manager; small savings agent.
